12.	On April 18, 1980, X formally gained independence from Britain. It had been a self-governing British colony since 1923. In 1965, its white-minority government under Ian Smith had unilaterally declared independence to avoid British demands for majority rule. This led to international sanctions and a prolonged guerrilla war waged by two liberation movements. When an agreement was finally reached and democratic elections held, the country adopted X as its new name. The old colonial name Y honored a British imperialist who had dreamed of a railway from Cape Town to Cairo. The new name comes from the ruins of a medieval stone city in the country's interior, whose name means "great houses of stone" in the Shona language. ID X (10 points) and Y (5 points).
